question.value: How are P-bearing molecules (PN, PO) formed in star-forming regions, and is the comet 67P/C-G P reservoir inherited from such environments?

evidence.quote: To understand how Phosphorus-bearing molecules are formed in star-forming regions, we have analysed ALMA observations of PN and PO towards the massive star-forming region AFGL 5142
as part of the project 2016.1.01071.S (PI: Rivilla)
The observations were performed in Band 3 with the array in the C40$-$3 configuration with baselines ranging from 15 to 460 m.

evidence.quote: The digital correlator was configured in 12 different spectral windows (spw’s) with channel widths of 122 kHz ($\sim$0.35 km s$^{-1}$)

baselines ranging from 15 to 460 m

analysis_steps.goal: Map SO, PN, PO emission and identify P-spots

method.value: Integrated maps in velocity ranges; seven P-spots identified visually in PN map

evidence.quote: peaking towards several visually-identified spots (P-spots, hereafter) located along the cavities of the bipolar outflow
three different velocity ranges (\[-6.5,-4.5\], \[-4.5,-2.0\] and \[-2.0, 0\] km s$^{-1}$)

method.value: Spectra from circular regions at P-spot, MM, HV positions

evidence.quote: The spectra extracted in a circular region of 3$^{\prime\prime}$ diameter centered on the positions of the P-spots

analysis_steps.goal: LTE fit of column densities, velocities, linewidths

method.value: MADCUBA-AUTOFIT synthetic LTE spectra with CDMS entries incl. 14N hyperfine

evidence.quote: we have used the MADCUBA-AUTOFIT tool that compares the observed spectra with the LTE synthetic spectra of the different species

key_parameters.value: Tex fixed: 5 K for PN/PO, 34 K for SO; free N, v, FWHM

evidence.quote: Then, fixing $T_{\rm ex}$, we run MADCUBA-AUTOFIT leaving $N$, $\varv$, and $FWHM$ as free parameters.

assumptions.value: LTE, single transition so Tex cannot be derived

evidence.quote: Since our data contain only a single rotational transition of the three species (PN, PO and SO), the excitation temperature cannot be derived, and hence we assumed fixed values.

fitting.value: Levenberg-Marquardt least squares; errors from covariance matrix

evidence.quote: This tool provides the best non-linear least-squared fit using the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm.

validation.value: Tex sensitivity: column densities vary by factor 2.5 (PN), 2.1 (PO) over 5-50 K

evidence.quote: the column densities of PN and PO can vary by a factor of 2.5 and 2.1, respectively, assuming different values of $T_{\rm ex}$ in the range of 5$-$50 K

method.value: RADEX with n(H2)=1e4,1e5,1e6 cm-3 deriving column densities matching line fluxes

evidence.quote: we have run RADEX assuming three different values: $n$(H$_2$) = 1$\times$10$^{4}$, 1$\times$10$^{5}$ and 1$\times$10$^{6}$ cm$^{-3}$.
The calculations assume a kinetic temperature of $T_{\rm kin}$ = 20 K and a background temperature of 2.73 K.

evidence.quote: In all cases, the PO/PN ratio clearly increases with increasing distance from the central protostar, supporting the role of photochemistry to explain the observed relative abundances of PN and PO.

findings_qualitative.value: PN and PO arise in low-velocity, narrow-line gas in outflow cavity walls, not at high-velocity outflow axis, hot core or starless core

evidence.quote: The ALMA maps show that the emission of PN and PO arises from several spots associated with low-velocity gas with narrow linewidths in the cavity walls of a bipolar outflow.

claims.experiment: Map PN/PO vs SO high-velocity gas
claims.result: No PN/PO at high-velocity SO positions; present in cavity walls

evidence.quote: This indicates that the mere presence of shocked material does not guarantee the detection of PO and PN.

claims.hypothesis: PO/PN ratio depends on UV exposure
claims.experiment: PO/PN versus distance from protostar via LTE and non-LTE

evidence.quote: In all cases, the PO/PN ratio clearly increases with increasing distance from the central protostar

claims.hypothesis: PO is main P carrier in comet 67P
claims.finding: PO is main carrier of P

evidence.quote: PO is indeed the main carrier of P in the comet, with PO/PN$>$10 and PO/PH$_3>$3.3.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Hot chemistry and high cosmic-ray ionization rate rejected for PO/PN ratios

evidence.quote: However, a high cosmic-ray ionisation rate is unlikely to be the reason of the PO/PN ratios observed.

limitations_admitted.value: Resolution too low to resolve cavity wall layers; speculative conclusions

evidence.quote: the current data only allows to draw some speculative conclusions, and higher angular resolution observations are needed

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-transition Tex assumed; column densities uncertain by factor ~2
Seven spots selected visually; PO/PN vs distance trend based on few points
Comet PO assignment relies on mass peak, ionization cross section assumed equal to NO
Photochemistry scenario qualitative, no source model
